Hi Evan —

Thanks for sending this along. We're happy to walk through each section; I reviewed the questionnaire and pulled together an evidence packet and some next steps. Summary answers below, full packet attached: redwood_slo_evidence_packet.zip

- Measurement: We calculate uptime as successful request rate over a rolling 30-day window (HTTP 200/2xx only). Latency SLOs use p95/p99 computed at the request level across the same rolling window. P99 is computed at the service edge after model routing and includes serialization time.

- Monitoring access: We can grant Brightwave a read-only Grafana role scoped to your account dashboards (no raw export by default). For customers that need metric exports we provide a metrics export job (CSV/Prometheus remote write) under a separate data-sharing agreement.

- Alerting: Customers may subscribe to alert webhooks or email thresholds. For on-call paging we recommend integrating our PagerDuty endpoint; customers can request per-route alert thresholds during onboarding.

- Temporary latency exception: We do have an exception path. For predictable daily batch windows we can document a calibrated exception (time window, expected p99 delta, mitigation steps) and record it in the customer playbook. Exceptions are timeboxed and require a brief architecture review and an agreed rollback policy.

Next actions:
1) I've attached the evidence packet (includes sample dashboards, SLO calculation notes, and a redacted incident timeline).
2) If Brightwave would like read-only Grafana access, confirm the primary reviewer email and we'll issue an invite.
3) If you want a temporary exception for the batch job, please tell us the recurring window (start/end in your timezone), expected request rate increase, and acceptable p99 value. We'll run a quick capacity check and propose controls (rate-limits, route weight shifts, fallback model).

If it's helpful, Marissa (who owns our uptime commitments) and Ben (who manages capacity and routing) are cc'ed and can join a short call.

Best,

Evan —

Thanks again for the details and for filling out the questionnaire. We reviewed the request with product and infra; summary of outcomes and next steps below.

1) Temporary onboarding exception approved (timeboxed):
   - Window: daily 02:00–02:45 UTC (documented in your onboarding playbook).
   - Allowed p99 delta: up to 900ms for the window. If p99 > 750ms for >5 minutes we will automatically shift traffic to the smaller fallback model and notify your ops contact.
   - Exception duration: initial trial for 14 days after go-live; renewable after post-trial review.

2) Monitoring & access: we issued a read-only Grafana invite scoped to Brightwave dashboards; link in portal and screenshot attached (grafana-invite-screenshot.png). Invite expires in 30 days — request extension if you need long-term access. Raw metric export can be put on a separate data-sharing addendum.

3) Alerting: we've set up a recommended PagerDuty integration with a per-route p99 threshold. We'll share the webhook instructions and a small runbook for on-call handling.

4) Billing/credits: the temporary exception does not change the SLA credit policy — credits apply only when the baseline SLO (outside exception windows) is missed. If the exception causes sustained degradation outside the agreed window we'll handle as standard.

Next steps:
- Priya will send the Grafana invite and the onboarding playbook entry.
- Evan, please confirm the Brightwave ops contact to receive alerts and whether you need the metrics export addendum.
- Ben will check routing weight thresholds and confirm fallback model and canary policy.
